No WY-specific override needed. A fee-shifting concern was raised 2026-08-28 (WY has no reciprocity statute per edu-no-fee-reciprocity-wy, so the clause's mutual "prevailing party" language is a voluntary giveaway; Taylor's decision: keep mutual language) then a stricter-standard flag was raised and RETRACTED 2026-09-06 after reading the actual case law: Cowardin v. Finnerty (Wyo. 1999); Emken, 2006 WY 112, ¶8; Thorkildsen v. Belden, 2012 WY 8; Circle Resources v. Hassler, 2023 WY 22, ¶8. WY standard is express contractual/statutory authorization (American Rule), not a heightened "unequivocal provision" test as this library's own edu-no-fee-reciprocity-wy row had mischaracterized it. This clause's express, named "prevailing party" language satisfies the real standard; no override required.

Self-limiting deferral to "the maximum amount allowed under applicable law" (shared-clause pass 2026-09-03 removed a hardcoded "double the Monthly Rent" figure that had no statutory basis in any of the 5 states then tagged, WY included). WY has no general prohibited-lease-provisions statute (confirmed by directly reading all 11 sections of Article 12). notes: Case law, not statute — WY is NOT among the 7 fee-reciprocity states (CA/FL/HI/MT/OR/UT/WA); WY follows the American Rule (31-state group per a Drake Law Review survey), no analog to C.R.S. §38-12-801(3)(a)(II). CORRECTED 2026-09-06: this row originally characterized the WY standard as requiring a contract to "unequivocally provide" for fee recovery — the cases actually require EXPRESS statutory or contractual authorization, a lower bar. The 2026-09-06 correction was a characterization fix only, not a full re-audit of this row's other holdings.

Wyoming has no holdover rent multiplier — holdover is grounds for a 3-day notice (§§1-21-1002(a)(i)/1003) and ordinary damages only. CORRECTED 2026-09-03 (primary-verified against wyoleg.gov and Justia): an earlier draft attributed a "10% interest" figure to §1211(b) as if it applied to holdover rent liability; §1211(b) actually governs PROPERTY DAMAGE, not holdover — a misapplied citation from a secondary source (PayRent) that had correctly cited the section but attached it to the wrong subject. The underlying negative (no holdover multiplier) is unaffected and is now stronger, resting on a full primary read of §1211 rather than the earlier misread provision.

Primary-verified (wyoleg.gov + Justia 2024 codification). Confirmed absence: no storage period, inventory duty, care duty, or pre-disposal notice requirement anywhere in Article 12 for a sheriff's post-writ removal of a tenant's possessions — a sharp contrast with Minnesota's §504B.365/§504B.271 (inventory, dual-channel notice, care standard, disposal tracks).

Secondary-sourced (apartments.com's structured WY chart returns "No statute" for all four tenancy-type categories; Nolo confirms no notice required to end a month-to-month tenancy). No WY case law fixing the common-law rule (one full rental period, ending at the start of a new period) was located — stated at practice-level confidence, not primary-source confidence. Distinguish the 3-day pre-suit eviction notice under §§1-21-1002/1003 (nonpayment/violation), which is NOT a periodic-tenancy termination-notice period.
